To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

silymarin and silybin-phosphatidylethanolamine complex are effective in prevention of dietary induced hyperlipidemia, and that silybin-phoshatidylethanolamin complex supresses LDL oxidizability more effectively than sialmarin.

the dietary supplementation of rats fed on high cholesterol diet with currant oil containing polyunsaturated and lower amounts of monounsaturated fatty acids improved the antihypercholestrolomic effect of silymarine, the extract from S. marianum L., but increased the oxidizability of low-density lipoprotein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of currant oil on the antihypercholes-terolemic and LDL-antioxidant effect of silymarins, and the improvement of silibinin bioavailability by phosphatidylcholin complexation.
the effects of silybin, a flavonolignane isolated from the milk thistle (Silybum marianus), on lipid metabolism and the oxidative stress of low density lipoprotein (LDL).
the modulation of the antihypercholeserolemic and LDL oxidizability effects of SM and SPC in rats fed on a HC-diet supplemented by the currant oil, the natural PUFA-rich source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
dietary supplementation of HC-diet with currant oil, rich in polyunsaturated fatty acid, improves antihyperchoesterolemic effect of silymarine, but induces an increased oxidation of LDL.

the dietary currant oil is effective in prevention of hypercholesterolema induced by HC-diet, but its use in prevention of atherosclerosis may be limited because it can induce increased LDL oxidizability, and the effect is more pronounced in rats fed on lard fat than in rats fed on currant oil.

silymarin and silibinin-phospatidylcholine have the potential for the prevention of hypercholesterolema in humans, and that silymarins may also have the ability to reduce the oxidative stress induced by dietary fats, but the effect depends on the composition of dietary fats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dietary currant oil is a good source of polyunsaturated fatty acid for prevention of development of diet-induced hypercholesterolema but the currant seed oil is a poor source of PUFA for LDL oxidation prevention.

dietary currant oil can be a good source for improvement of antihyperlipidemic effects of silybin, but the currants oil-induced increase of LDL oxidation can be prevented by improvement of bioaccessibility and bioavailability of silbin by complexation with phosphatidylcholines.

the dietary supplementation with currant oil improves the antihypercholes-terolemic effect of silymarine, but the increased oxidizabil-ity of LDL induced by currant oil can be prevented by the improvement of silibinin bioavailability, as shown here with silibinin-phophatidylcholne complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that

dietary PUFA can modulate the effect of silymarins on the lipid metabolism in rats fed on hypercholesterolemiagenic diet, and that silibinin-phospatidylcholine is a better bioavailable form of silibinin.
the currant oil can improve the antihypercholestrolemic effect of silymarins, but it can increase LDL oxidizability and thus the risk of atherosclerosis.
dietary fat, as the main component of the HC diet, has a significant influence on the effects of SM and SPC on plasma cholesterol and LDL oxidizability.
